April 2010 # Looking for the green shoots of recovery - Spot cathode demand is picking up in Europe and the USA, partly due to seasonal factors but we also believe some consumers may have been caught short. Asian demand is still strong, but there is now a little less optimism about China than at the start of the year. - Cathode production continues to surprise on the high side, despite recent events that usually would lead to a loss of production, not least the Chilean earthquake. - The copper price has been range bound and unable to breach $7,600/t. Barring any significant disruption to production or an unexpectedly strong rise in Chinese imports that would boost prices, we expect prices to be supported above $7,000/t. # Spot demand picks up 

Copper prices began to test the $7,000/t level at the time of writing the last Monitor, which was just prior to the Chilean earthquake.  The quake on 27<sup>th</sup> February provided the impetus to push prices higher, however as the damage to the country’s mines was minimal the upside to the price recovery was capped.  The intraday 3-month price reached a high of $7,625/t on 3<sup>rd</sup> March, below the recent January highs.  In March prices have edged lower, averaging just over $7,400/t up to the time of writing.  Price changes have been driven mainly by sentiment in response to macroeconomic developments and movements in the value of the US dollar, rather than copper market specific factors. 

From a fundamental perspective, we have confirmed **3000** that Chinese consumption has picked up since the New **2500 Jan-09 Mar-09 May-09 Jul-09 Aug-09 Oct-09 Dec-09 Feb-10** Year holiday.  In addition, other Asian countries are also Data: LME seeing a continuation of the solid consumption growth noted last month.  In the mature markets of North America and Europe, although we are now entering a period of seasonally stronger demand, the upturn has been modest so far.  It has, however, been sufficient to halt the upward trend in exchange stock inventories at just short of 800,000 tonnes in early March.  Meanwhile, refined production remains quite robust, with minimal disruptions, but we still expect to see a global deficit in Q2. 

### **Spot demand up somewhat in Europe and USA, premiums little changed** 

Last month we highlighted the strength of refined copper consumption in Asia, a story that has not changed much over the past month.  What has changed is confirmation of an uptick in demand for and consumption of refined copper in Europe and the USA.  The upturn is modest, with spot activity more muted in the USA compared to Europe.  The upturn in the US appears to be in part due to the lack of scrap in the country, with scrap discounts having fallen to 24-29¢/lb this month from 35-45¢/lb in Q4 2009.  Traders in the USA are seeing small volume business from customers who usually consume scrap as their raw material of choice, but cannot source enough scrap at the moment so are topping up with refined feed.  However, this is not the sole reason for increased cathode demand, with electrical and electronic end-use sectors in particular driving an upturn in consumption by semi fabricators serving these markets.  Construction, which is one of the biggest drivers of seasonality, both directly and indirectly, remains in the doldrums.  Residential activity is low and recent data releases paint a gloomy outlook for 2010, although the bad weather early in 2010 has accounted for some of the recent weakness.  The overhang of excess commercial property continues to be a drag on copper demand from the construction sector, with few new projects outside those funded by stimulus expenditure. This increased activity saw a widening

of the top end of the range of premiums in the US, with deals reported as high as 4.5¢/lb up from 4.0¢/lb last month.  The increase is mostly down to the small volumes required necessitating truck delivery and therefore higher freight charges. 

In Europe, the increased spot market activity is in part due to the sequential increase in refined consumption, which we expect to be 11% higher in H1 2010 than it was in H2 2009.  As in the USA, semi fabricators supplying the electrical and electronic sectors are seeing increased consumption.  However, there are also some indications that semis plants that had been cautious in their annual contracts with producers and rolled over commitments from 2009 into early 2010 may have used up all that material and have had to come back into the

spot market.  Nevertheless, the activity has not yet reached sufficient volumes to shift the trading range for spot cathode premiums, which have stayed at $60-80/t. 

### **Asian consumption maintaining strength** 

As usual, China dominates the copper market story.  Chinese consumption growth following the Spring Festival last month has been less robust than some market participants in China had been hoping.  The arbitrage window has been largely closed for the past month and the spot premium for imported cathode has eased back further, to below $100/t.  The premium is down due to the low number of transactions, as consumers remain cautious about cathode purchases.  March imports will be above February, but the lower import premium and closing of the arbitrage window indicate that the physical market in China appears to be well supplied, so refined imports in April and May could be lower than in February and March.  In February, net Chinese supply of cathode from refined imports and refined production in China rose by 39,000t (+12.8%) m-o-m.  However, the rise in visible SHFE stocks more than offset this increase in supply, leading to apparent demand, calculated using available data, falling slightly last month.  Real copper consumption was up last month compared to January, as we have heard anecdotal evidence in China that some of the off warrant stocks in the country were released to the market.  However, the loss of working days due to the Spring Festival holiday means that the increase was modest at best. 

The biggest downside threat to the consumption outlook in China remains the impact of the Central Bank’s efforts to rein in credit growth.  However, one positive for copper is that the central government has confirmed that all subsidy schemes, including the rural home appliance, automotive and agricultural equipment schemes, will continue in 2010.  This suggests that there should be downstream support for copper demand, especially for wirerod and flat rolled products.  Nonetheless, the current outlook remains less optimistic than it was at the start

of the year.  The target GDP growth rate has been set at 8%, which implies a sharp slowdown from the 11% y-o-y recorded in Q4 2009.  CRU believes there will be a slowdown in GDP, but that it will be less than the government target.  We expect that the annual GDP growth rate for 2010 will be 10%.  This deceleration will filter through to semis production, which we expect will average about 10% for the year as a whole.  The slowdown in copper semis demand growth will likely be focussed on the credit sensitive sectors of construction and infrastructure. 

### **Scrap continuing to result in higher refined demand, but less than last year** 

The scrap market continues to be tight, with discounts sharply lower, reflecting subdued generation and strong demand from China.  As mentioned earlier, in the US we are hearing that the tight availability is forcing smaller fabricators, who normally consume scrap, to enter the spot cathode market to meet their requirements. In China, February scrap imports fell for the second straight month.  We believe this reflects the week long holiday last month, rather than a fundamental decline in demand.  Looking ahead, the Chinese customs service have announced that they will require importers to declare the grade of scrap shipments on customs documents. Historically China has seen much misreporting of scrap grades to evade duties and VAT.  So the implementation of this change is likely to negatively impact Chinese scrap import volumes in April and possibly May, in the same way as increased inspections last year delayed scrap imports.  The supply of domestically generated scrap should grow this year, due to the home appliance schemes, but the increase will be modest.  Overall, we estimate that there will be a positive impact on refined demand in China from the lack of scrap in the country, though only by about 100-150,000t t compared to last year’s 400-500,000t. 

### **Exchange stock rise topping out** 

The rise in exchange stocks seen over the past six months ended in early-March.  Comex stocks stopped rising in early-February and LME stocks in mid-February.  Total exchange stocks, though, did not follow until earlyMarch, as over the past two months SHFE stocks rose above the roughly 100,000t level they had been at for several months to 169,101t as of 18th March.  The rise on SHFE has subsided over the last couple of weeks,

but so has the rate of decline in LME stocks, so overall we are really only seeing exchange stocks plateau at a high level.  With the market moving into deficit, we expect to see exchange stocks decline over the next few months, even in the USA, where demand is weakest. 

Europe has been left with relatively low stocks moving into the seasonally stronger Q2 and are now below 75,000t following withdrawals of about 20,000t since mid-February.  We estimate that this decline is greater th

an the uptick in demand in the region and some of the withdrawals are likely due to warrant holders moving material out of LME warehouses ahead of the 1st April warehousing price increase. That said, the consensus is that offwarrant stocks are also at a low level. Therefore, if consumption is stronger than expected and/or there is a disruption to supply, Europe is currently the region most exposed to a jump in premiums. Rise in exchange

### **Production continues to see few disruptions despite recent events** On the supply side, there continue to be few disruptions at mine, smelters and refineries. As has been widely reported, the Chile earthquake had little immediate impact on copper production in the country. However, the consequences of the earthquake are expected to disrupt copper production in the coming months. Infrastructure that was not severely damaged by the earthquakes is still at risk from further damage given the additional tremors. This includes power and oil refining facilities, which is significant as the country was already suffering from energy shortages. Nevertheless, there are likely to be several minor disruptions across the supply chain from the quake, such as the damage to the two steel mills in the country that make the steel balls used in grinding operations. These mills are currently out of action. Imported steel balls are available from China but the quality is inferior and could therefore result in lower throughput. These kinds of issues are the sorts of things that will likely be a drag on production growth in Chile in the months ahead. Meanwhile, Boliden expects to make up all of the lost production following the closure of its smelting and refining operations in Finland due to a lack of concentrates as a result of a two week port strike in the country. We do not expect that the closure of Grupo Mexico’s San Luis Potosi smelter will impact global production either, as Chinese smelting expansions continue apace and will keep the pressure on smelters in other regions by supporting low TC/RCs. This latest smelter closure is really only an example of further smelting rationalisation, and follows on from Xstrata’s announcement in December 2009 of the closure of Kidd Creek on 1st May this year. ### **Prices to be supported by fundamentals, but dollar could be a constraint** Overall, the move into a deficit market in Q2 should support copper prices. W|orld Adj|usted prod|uction inc|ludes| © 2010 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 7 of 12 Copper Monitor April 2010 www.crumonitor.com # Consumption trends: ## **Copper flat rolled products demand in 2009 fell towards 2003 levels** Copper flat rolled products include copper and copper alloy plate, sheet, strip and foil as well as electro deposited copper foil (ED foil). The primary endmarkets for copper flat rolled products are the electrical and electronic products and consumer and general products sectors. Our estimates show that world consumption of all copper and copper alloy foil and flat rolled products declined by 11.0% y-o-y to 3.5M tonnes. All regions saw volumes of copper plate, sheet and strip decline, dropping 15.6% y-o-y to 1.4 million tonnes in 2009, with the largest slump in the Americas (-34.3%) and Europe (-23.5%). Asia remained relatively resilient, with Developing Asia increasing by 0.6% y-o-y but North East Asia fell by 26.6% y-o-y. Total copper alloy plate, sheet, strip and foil demand was 7.7% lower in 2009, compared to 1.9 million tonnes in 2008. The decline in consumption was again mainly due to sharply lower offtake in the Western World, and in both North American and Western Europe in par

ticular. Demand and trade in copper plate, sheet and strip have been vulnerable to the deterioration in the residential and commercial construction sectors over the past few years. The high price of copper has driven substitution of roofing strip (pure copper) to other materials such as stainless steel or titanium strip. Total of LM E, COM EX, and Shanghai Futures © 2010 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 9 of 12 Copper Monitor April 2010 www.crumonitor.com # Industry News # Mine Production - On 27th February, a 8.8 magnitude earthquake shook the central and southern regions of **Chile** . Copper operations have not suffered any major damage, but those located near Santiago ( **El Teniente** , **Andina** , **E** l **Soldado** , **Los Bronces** and **Mantoverde** mines; and **Chagres, El Teniente** and **Ventanas** smelters) halted production for few days mainly due to power cuts. The earthquake was followed by several aftershocks and a 6.3 earthquake near Calama (northern regions). In addition, on Sunday 14th March, a blackout in **Chile** affected about 80-90% of the country. Mining operations reported minor or no disruptions. In 2009, 3.25Mt of copper-in-concentrates and 2.11Mt of EW cathode were produced in Chile. - In mid-March, it was reported that the **Huachipato** plant – the only producer of steel bars in Chile – suffered severe damages as a result of the earthquake and the company decided to close the plant for 3 months. Agents in the mining industry believe that **Moly-Cop** , **Proacer** and other producers have stocks but these are understood to be committed to Codelco. Miners have started to look for alternative suppliers in Peru, Brazil, China and Australia. - On 1st March, **Rio Tinto** announced that they agreed to buy 15M shares at C$16.31 per share (C$244.7M in total, approx US$240M) of **Ivanhoe Mines** . This will increase Rio Tinto’s interest in Ivanhoe Mines by 2.7% to 22.4%. Ivanhoe Mines has the **Oyu Tolgoi** project in Mongolia, which is expected to start-up in 2013 and produce 436,000t/y of copper-in-concentrate at full capacity. - On 22nd March, **Quadra Mining** announced their intention to merge with **FNX Mining Company** to create a new mid-tier company called **Quadra FNX Mining** . Quadra Mining could pay around C$1.6B (~US$1.57B) accor

ding to current stock values.  In 2009, Quadra Mining produced 21,000t of EW cathode and 56,000t of copper-in-concentrate. 



- **Antofagasta Minerals** said that the commissioning of the **Los Pelambres** expansion has been delayed and will now be completed during Q2 2010 (instead of Q1 as planned).  The commissioning of **Esperanza** is also delayed and will start in Q4 2010 due to the impact of the earthquake on some facilities and logistics.  In 2009, Los Pelambres produced 322,600t of copper-in-concentrates. Esperanza is projected to produce 191,000t/y of copper-in-concentrates at full capacity. 



- On 17<sup>th</sup> March, **Newmont** announced that its subsidiary, **Newmont Indonesia Limited** , together with **Nusa Tenggara Mining Corporation BV** ("NTMC"), an affiliate of Sumitomo, had completed the sale of 7% of PT Newmont Nusa Tenggara ("PTNNT") corresponding to the PTNNT 2009 divestiture obligations. The 7% interest was sold to **PT Multi Daerah Bersaing** , a consortium comprised of regional and local governments near the **Batu Hijau** copper-gold mine in Indonesia, and PT Multicapital, a private company.  The transaction was worth US$247M.  In 2010, Batu Hijau is expected to produce 210,000t of copper-in-concentrate. 



- In mid-March it was reported that an agreement was reached over a new collective labour contract at **Codelco Norte** ( **Chuquicamata** , **Radomiro Tomic** and **Mina Sur** ) with a union of over 500 workers.  It is understood that workers asked for a 5% pay rise, a 35-month contract and other benefits for the Calama and Mejillones cities, but details of the final agreement have not been

## **Exploration and Development** 



- On 1<sup>st</sup> March, Canada's **Chariot Resource** announced an arrangement with **China** S **ci** - **Tech** under which the latter will acquire all of the issued and outstanding common shares of the former.  Chariot Resources owns the **Mina Justa** copper project in Peru that will probably start-up in 2018 and produce an average of 62,000t/y of copper-in-concentrates. 



- On 8<sup>th</sup> March, **Quadra Mining** announced a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) to form a joint venture with **State Grid International Development Limited** ("SGID"), a wholly owned subsidiary of **State Grid Corporation of China** , the largest Chinese utility company and a major end user of copper.  The joint venture will develop and operate Quadra's *

*Sierra Gorda** project and **Franke** mine in Chile, as well as invest in other prospective copper assets, initially in Chile. The parties will be entitled to their proportionate share of the concentrate or cathode production of the JV.  Quadra will be responsible for the operational aspects and SGID for the project financing.  Sierra Gorda is expected to start-up in 2014 and produce 139,000t of copper-in-concentrate at full capacity. Franke produced 8,000t of EW cathode in 2009 and is still ramping-up. 



- It has been reported that **Pan Pacific Copper** (JV of **Nippon Mining** & **Metals** and **Mitsui Mining** & **Smelting** ) have confirmed that they are to develop the **Caserones** project (Chile).  The project is expected to start-up in 2013 and will produce an average of 150,000t/y of copper-in-concentrates. 

## **Smelting and Refining** 



- Several smelters are due to close for care and maintenance in the coming months.  These include: **Codelco’s Ventanas** (20-25-days, due to resume operations soon), **PPC’s Tamano** (1-month in Mar/Apr), **Kosaka** (3-weeks in August) and **Mitsubishi Materials’ Gresik** (20-days in May). 



- In early March, it was reported that **Mitsubishi Materials** will run their smelters at full capacity from April to September this year.  This would put an end to their temporary production cutbacks.  In 2009, Mitsubishi Materials produced 190,000t of copper blister. 



- It has been reported that **Freeport-McMoRan Copper & Gold Inc** ’s Indonesian unit, which operates **Grasberg** , aims to sell more copper concentrate to local smelters, in line with the new Indonesian law which requires miners to either process concentrates in the country or send them to local smelters.  However, talks with local smelters have stalled and due to the currently limited levels of Indonesian smelting capacity the new regulation cannot be implemented immediately.   The company sells around 30% of Grasberg’s copper concentrates to the Indonesian smelter at Gresik, in which Freeport has a 25% share.  In 2009, Grasberg produced 771,000t of copper-in-concentrates. 



- New investments in Chinese smelting and refining capacity continue.  The **Lianyungang government** and **Jiangsu Huanqiu Copper Co** have announced a joint investment in a 800,000t/y smelter and refinery in Lianyungang.  Phase 1 is due to be completed by the end of 2011, with a

## **Consumption** 



- **Furukawa Electric Group** has announced that it will start operation in April at its new ¥1.2bn (US$13.3m) winding wire factory, which is being built at the **Riken Electric Wire** Shirone factory site (in Niigata, Japan).  Production will be transferred from **Totoku Electric** ’s Maruko factory (in Nagano) – the equipment move should be complete by end-H1 of fiscal 2010.  The new factory will have a production capacity of 500t/m, and will manufacture high value-added products for electronics such as alloy wire and ultra extra fine wire.
